master.title: BANGLADESH: Daily Press Review (30 Oct. 2023)
master.content:
The Delegation of the European Union to Bangladesh
Produced by Political, Trade, Press and Information Section

 

EU deeply saddened to see deaths, violence on Dhaka streets (The New Age): The European Union and its member states in Bangladesh on Sunday said that they were deeply saddened as they had to see deaths and violence on Dhaka streets. The EU made the remarks in a post on X, formerly twitter, at around noon. The European Union and its Member States in Dhaka are deeply saddened to see the loss of life and violence on the streets of Dhaka - vital that a peaceful way forward for participatory and peaceful elections is found, the social media post read. Also in: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, The Business Standard

 

Seminar on Smart Grid: Shaping the Future of Sustainable Energy held in Dhaka (UNB): A seminar highlighting the smart grid solution and empowering the future of power distribution was held in Dhaka recently to get more innovative ideas for accelerating the Smart Grid project. Under the Construction and Augmentation of Substation Installation of Capacitor Bank and Introduction of Smart Grid in Power System under DPDC Areas (CSCSG Project) initiated by Dhaka Power Distribution Company Limited (DPDC) and co-funded by the European Union (EU) and AFD, the seminar was held to discover the endless possibilities of smarter energy future. The seminar titled Exploring Smart Grids, Shaping the Future of Sustainable Energy was held at University of Asia Pacific (UAP) and was organised by DPDC, said a media release on Sunday. Also in: The Financial Express, The Business Standard, The Daily Sun, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune

 

Bangladesh demands immediate end of Israeli brutalities (The New Age): Bangladesh has strongly condemned the slaying of innocent civilians including women and children and demanded an immediate end to Israeli brutalities in Palestine, according to a statement by the country s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued on Sunday. It said Bangladesh played a significant role in organising an emergency special session of the UN General Assembly on the Palestine situation and co-sponsored the resolution adopted in the session held on 27 October 2023, with two-thirds majority, calling for a humanitarian truce in Gaza. The General Assembly asked Israel to stop its attempts to forcibly transfer the Palestinian civilian population and called for the immediate and unconditional release of all civilians who are being held captive illegally.

 

Ex-CEC of India backs Bangladesh Election Commission to hold fair polls (Dhaka Tribune): SY Quraishi, former chief election commissioner of India, has said he believes that the Election Commission of Bangladesh can hold free and fair polls. The commission held a meeting with nine representatives, including election commissioners of India, Maldives, Sri Lanka and Nepal and Election Monitoring Forum, at Nirbachan Bhabn in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Sunday. Quraishi s comment to reporters came after that meeting. The Bangladesh Election Commission has all the powers to make an election free and fair. I see no reason not to trust them. Some of the past elections have been one-sided, and there may be a question about their acceptance because of this, Quraishi said.

 

EC secretary finds conditions favourable for election schedule announcement (Dhaka Tribune): Election Commission Secretary Md Jahangir Alam has said conditions are now favourable for the announcement of the schedule for the upcoming general election, stating that the polls will be held within 90 days before the expiration of the current parliament s 5-year term in line with the constitution, and the commission is finalizing its preparations. The Election Commission held a meeting with election commissioners from India, Maldives, Sri Lanka and Nepal, and nine representatives, including those from Election Monitoring Forum, at Nirbachan Bhaban in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Sunday morning. Four election commissioners, including Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Kazi Habibul Awal, attended the meeting.

 

EMF calls for participatory election (The Daily Star): The upcoming parliamentary election should be participatory, said the Election Monitoring Forum (EMF) yesterday. It is a polls watchdog consisting of incumbent and former EC from neighbouring countries. EMF Director Prof Abdul Jabbar Khan called on the government to initiate a dialogue with political parties e after an EMF delegation met the election commissioners of Bangladesh at the EC office. India's former CEC SY Quraishi, Chairman of the Maldives Election Commission Fuwad Thowfeek, Chairman of the EC of Sri Lanka RMAL Rathnayake, Nepal EC Sagun Shamsher JB Rana, and former commissioner Ila Sharma, among others, were part of the delegation.

 

BNP wasn't prepared for such an incident (Prothom Alo): Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) had no preparation for any incident where the government would resort to provocation to foil their grand rally  in a planned manner, even after giving them permission, BNP leaders have said. BNP had a plan to set a final date for the resignation for the government at the grand rally, but that has not been possible. Before speeches by important leaders including the chief guest, the grand rally was foiled by attacks and clashes.

 

Govt takes hard line against BNP (The Daily Star): Fakhrul arrested, sent to jail in vandalism case; many top leaders sued; 960 held across country; The government appears to have taken a tough stance against the BNP after Saturday's clashes that turned the heart of the capital into a battlefield. BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sent to jail by a Dhaka court around 10:00pm yesterday. Detectives picked him up from his Gulshan home around 9:25am. Police last night said he was arrested in a case filed with Ramna Police Station over Saturday's attack on the residence of the chief justice in Kakrail.

 

Violence, deaths, arson mar hartal; BNP announces three-day blockade from 31 Oct (The Business Standard): Port operations slowed, banking transactions decreased significantly; The resumption of political hartal in Bangladesh brought sporadic violence and unrest across the country, with incidents including arson attacks on buses and clashes with police, resulting in three deaths on Sunday. The disruptions also impacted economic activities with port operations experiencing a slowdown and transactions in banks decreasing significantly during the hartal, enforced by the opposition BNP and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. Amid all this, BNP has announced nationwide blockades for three days starting 31 October. Garment factories, crucial to the nation's economy, continued their operations during yesterday's hartal. Workers near Ashulia, Gazipur, and Savar reported to work with ease.

 

BNP, allies call 3-day blockade across Bangladesh from Tuesday (The New Age): The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Sunday announced a three-day blockade programme across the country to press home its demand for the resignation of the ruling Awami League government and to protest against Saturday s police at the party s grand rally in Dhaka. After observing a day-long strike across the country on Sunday, BNP senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said in a virtual press conference that a complete blockade programme would be enforced on October 31, November 1, and November 2. To protect the livelihood of the people who are affected by the ongoing rise in commodity prices due to ongoing injustice, mismanagement, unlimited corruption, lawlessness, money laundering, and syndicates, the attack on the October 28 grand rally, the killing of leaders and workers, and the arrest of BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, BNP will hold this programme for the next three days, he said.

 

Three killed in clashes, arson attacks during hartal (The Daily Star): Dozens hurt, 7 vehicles torched; Three people were killed and around two dozens injured during yesterday's nationwide dawn-to-dusk hartal of the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami. There were clashes in several districts and at least seven vehicles were torched and 15 others vandalised. A bus helper who was sleeping inside a bus was killed after arsonists set the vehicle alight early yesterday in Demra. An Awami League activist was stabbed to death during a clash in Lalmonirhat while a BNP leader fell to his death from a building when he was being chased by a mob in the capital's Mohammadpur.

 

Home minister holds BNP central leaders accountable for recent violence (Dhaka Tribune): Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan on Sunday said the BNP s central leaders cannot avoid responsibility for the arson, damage to lives and properties and disorder carried out by BNP men in Dhaka a day earlier. He was responding to a question from journalists at a peace rally organized by the local Awami League unit in protest of terrorism and anarchy by BNP-Jamaat in Araihazar upazila of Narayanganj. The home minister alleged that the BNP has unleashed arson similar to what it did in 2014 in the country. Today they (BNP) burnt buses in Demra. Yesterday they carried out attacks on the chief justice s house as well as vehicles, killing police and beating up journalists. Their central leaders will have to take responsibility [for these acts], he said.

 

14-party alliance to hold protest rally Monday (Dhaka Tribune): Awami League-led 14-party alliance will hold a protest rally on Monday to protest the attacks on police, journalists and vandalizing the residence of the Chief Justice in the capital. The rally will be held at the central office of Awami League in Bangabandhu Avenue at 3pm, said a press release signed by Awami League Secretary Sayem Khan on Sunday. According to the press release, Awami League advisory council member and 14-party alliance coordinator Amir Hossain Amu will preside over the rally.

 

No dialogue before upcoming polls: Quader (The Daily Star): Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader today said there won't be any dialogue before the upcoming election unless the BNP agrees with the "four settled issues". "The four issues are settled -- no caretaker government will be formed, Sheikh Hasina will be the prime minister of the election-time government, the parliament will be in the status quo, and no change will come in the election commission," he said at a press briefing in the AL president's Dhanmondi office. He also said there is no scope for BNP's involvement in the election-time government as there is no elected member of parliament from this party.

 

696 arrested in 28 cases over Oct 28 violence: DMP (The Daily Star): In the aftermath of yesterday's BNP-police clashes, a total of 28 cases have been filed with 21 police stations of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP). Md Faruk Hossain, deputy commissioner (media) of the DMP, said police have thus far apprehended 696 individuals in connection with these cases. From October 21 to October 28, a total of 1,480 individuals were arrested by the DMP for their involvement in acts of sabotage and violations of law and order.

 

Editors' Council slams attacks on journalists (The New Age): The Editors' Council, a platform for newspaper editors in Bangladesh, expressed deep concern and condemnation on Sunday over the attacks on journalists during the political programmes in Dhaka on Saturday. In a statement signed by Mahfuz Anam and Dewan Hanif Mahmud, the group said that as part of their professional duties, journalists collect news and present it to the public. But it is very worrying that the journalists are attacked or their security is disrupted when they are performing their duties. On October 28, around 25 journalists were injured or attacked in different parts of the capital while performing their professional duties, which is highly condemnable and worrying, reads the statement.

 

BFUJ, DUJ give BNP-Jamaat 72 hours to apologize to assaulted journalists (Dhaka Tribune): The Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) and Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ) issued a 72-hour ultimatum that said they would boycott all news related to BNP-Jamaat if they no not apologive to journalists who were attacked during Saturday s rally. BFUJ and DUJ organized a protest rally in front of the National Press Club on Sunday. The leaders of the organizations said they would also withhold the publication of any positive news about BNP Vice Chairman Tarique Rahman.

 

Trade unions demand quick announcement (The Daily Star): Trade union leaders of the garment sector yesterday urged the government to announce a "decent" minimum wage for workers as soon as possible to prevent workers from engaging in further agitations. Workers of different garment factories in Ashulia, Gazipur and Savar areas have been agitating over the last few days demanding that the government announce an "acceptable" salary as soon as possible. The leaders of the trade unions and federations of trade unions said the agitations were also in demand of salary arrears.

 

New RMG wage structure to take effect from 1 December: Monnujan Sufian (The Business Standard): Readymade garment workers' new wage structure will be finalised by 30 November and in effect from 1 December this year, State Minister for Labour and Employment Begum Monnujan Sufian said on Sunday (29 October). She made this announcement at an emergency meeting with the trade union and federation leaders at Shromo Bhavan over the ongoing situation in the industrial zones. "We called you to uncover the backstory behind the ongoing strike," she said, raising questions, "Are there any benefits for workers in a vandalised workplace? Ensuring peace in the workplace is key to positive outcomes for employees."

 

-End-
